hn-50122800.s: The decades-old mystery of the origins of one of the most popular cryptographic standards has been explained.
ex: “It’s just timestamps”: the decades-old mystery of the origins of one of the most popular cryptographic standards has been explained. We pursued this long-standing open question of the cryptographic community to settle concerns about ECDSA, which is one of our most widely used cryptographic standards. Readers should take this as a fun closing chapter and the end of years of speculation. There is no action to be taken or things to do differently. Most researchers trusted the curves already. Enjoy. ECDSA is the most widely used elliptic curve cryptography standard. It was adopted by NIST in 2000 as part of the FIPS 186-2 Digital Signature Standard which lists a set of standard elliptic curves of varying sizes and security levels. For curves over prime and binary fields, the specifications published a “seed” parameter whose hash value is used to define the coefficient b of the curve.

hn-50129121.s: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 is the October 17, 2026 snapshot of DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, served by DeepSeek under the `deepseek-flash` API model name.
ex: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 is the October 17, 2026 snapshot of DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, served by DeepSeek under the deepseek-flash API model name. V4.1 Flash is a sparse mixture-of-experts model from DeepSeek, and the first built on the company's Causal Encoder-Decoder (CED) architecture. It activates 8B parameters on input and 16B on output from a 552B-parameter backbone, an asymmetric split that keeps per-token compute low relative to the model's total size. Image understanding is native to the architecture, with visual and text embeddings trained jointly from the start of pre-training rather than added afterward as in the earlier experimental V4 Flash Vision ExpOpens in new tab. It is suited for coding, terminal, and computer-use agents, along with long-horizon tasks that must run to completion across many steps and long-context analysis. Compressed KV caching cuts cache memory to roughly a quarter of the previous Flash generation, significantly reducing costs on agentic workloads.

hn-50121179.t: 90% of US working hours are spent on tasks not covered well by AI benchmarks
hn-50121179.s: The US Benchmark Map places AI benchmarks across the American economy, measuring which parts of the labor force are covered by unsaturated, public, agentic benchmarks.
ex: AI benchmarks have multiplied in recent years, but coverage of economically valuable work remains limited. To measure this, we compiled relevant benchmarks to measure their coverage of American jobs. This Benchmark Map is our first step toward building a comprehensive, continuously updated resource for understanding AI capabilities across the economy. Each tile represents one of the 923 O*NET occupations making up the US labor force, grouped into 22 job families. Occupations are shaded according to the share of their tasks which are represented in our initial list of AI benchmarks. A single benchmark prompt can be mapped to multiple O*NET tasks. In our data set: only 208 of 923 occupations have a task with at least 5 benchmark prompts, and 6 of 22 job families have no such occupations. Our findings suggest that 90% of American working hours are spent on tasks with little or no coverage from existing benchmarks.

hf-deepseek-ai-DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017.s: We’re on a journey to advance and democratize artificial intelligence through open source and open science.
ex: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 is a minor update to DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, delivering substantial improvements across reasoning, coding, agentic tasks, and visual benchmarks. Alongside these gains, the model reduces task execution time and output length, enabling users to complete tasks faster and at lower cost and advancing the performance–cost Pareto frontier across multiple agent harnesses. † denotes the text-only subset of HLE. We use the Claude Code harness for Terminal-Bench 4.0 and the Mini-SWE-V2 harness for DeepSWE v1.1. This release does not include a Jinja-format chat template. The encoding folder contains a self-contained Python reference implementation (encoding.py) with test cases for multi-turn conversations, tool calling, thinking mode, numeric reasoning effort, mid-conversation system messages, and interleaved image content.

hn-50122431.t: Llama.cpp on a jailbroken PS5: run any GGUF model natively on the console
hn-50122431.s: llama.cpp on a jailbroken PS5: run any GGUF model natively on the console, starting with Qwen 3.8
ex: PS5LM is for anyone with a jailbroken PS5 who wants a private model server at home. It loads a GGUF model onto the console's GPU and serves it to your laptop, your phone and your coding tools. It needs no PC while it runs, no cloud and no account. - It runs on the GPU. llama.cpp's Vulkan backend on the console's RDNA 2 GPU, with 11.4 GB of the shared memory for the model and its context. Every architecture and quantization llama.cpp knows comes along. - It answers your network. OpenAI's /v1/chat/completions, Anthropic's /v1/messages (Claude Code works against it) and a chat page in any browser. Point a client at http:// :8081 and use any model name: the loaded one answers. - It decides, too. Load a decision model and the console answers TypeSafe's /v1/systemone: choice, score and yes-or-no questions about text and images, the API Ollaya serves on a PC. - It shows its work. Every request streams across the TV as a chat: which device asked, what it asked, and the reply as it is written.

hn-50122878.t: You could have invented transformers from memory
hn-50122878.s: Large language models today can recall obscure facts from every corner of the world. Most recently, I was running late for a friend’s board game night, so I asked Astra to remind me the rules to…
ex: Large language models today can recall obscure facts from every corner of the world. Most recently, I was running late for a friend’s board game night, so I asked Astra to remind me the rules to Dune: Imperium. It gladly narrated them to me as I drove over and helped me remember the rules well enough for me to play again. We’re so used to asking models about anything that we take their vast knowledge for granted. How do models remember so much information? And how much can they store? In this post, I’ll go through an intuitive way to look at linear maps, MLPs, and self-attention as different kinds of memory stores. From this intuition we can derive some heuristics for how much memory each layer can store. The key property that characterizes a “good” memory store is its ability to recall what it stored. After all, even if we could store infinitely many facts, it’s not very helpful if we can’t recall them when we need to.

hn-50131189.t: Esp32sim – Run ESP32 firmware in the browser
hn-50131189.s: Open-source ESP32 emulator. Run real firmware locally or in your browser — no hardware, no cloud, no subscription.
ex: esp32sim is an ESP32 emulator written in Rust. It runs real ESP32 firmware on your computer or in a browser tab, without the hardware. It boots the chip's own mask ROM, the real second-stage bootloader and your unmodified application. It also models the board around the chip: displays, touch, LEDs, buttons, audio, camera and WiFi. Try it in your browser, nothing to install: https://mikroverk.github.io/esp32sim/ - The full boot chain: mask ROM, bootloader, FreeRTOS, then your app. No patched firmware. - WiFi with the unmodified Espressif WiFi library. Firmware joins a virtual access point, gets DHCP, DNS and NTP, and can reach the real network, HTTPS included. - Board models, so firmware can draw on a display, read touch, light LEDs and play sound. - Speed: the S3 has a block cache and a JIT, and runs helloworld about 30 times faster than real time. - A WebAssembly build of the same emulator for the browser.

In fact, 7.2 was one of the busiest development cycles in the kernel's history, adding nearly 600,000 lines of code. hn-50118688.s: StarSkirmish: where LLMs write code to play StarCraft.
ex: The StarSkirmish Bench evaluates how strong of a StarCraft bot can each LLM write given 1 hour of wall clock time. v0.2 updates StarSkirmish Bench v0.1 with flagship models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta, each running in its lab's 1st party CLI harness. An LLM’s score reflects its win rate against a roster of competitive human written bots and demo bots. 1 hour runs, in its 1st party CLI harness. Scores are average win rates (0–100) of each model's 5 runs against a roster of competitive human written bots. Gemini 4 Argon runs at high, the highest reasoning effort available to it; every other model runs at max. GPT-6 Astra is the top scoring StarSkirmish Bench v0.2 LLM, a clear step ahead of GPT-6.1 Sol in second. Gemini 4 Argon, Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Fable 5.1 are functionally tied behind them, all scoring between 37 and 39. StarSkirmish Bench score against the average API cost of one 1 hour run. Cost is on a log scale.

hn-50121939.t: Designing more efficient quantum circuits with Claude
hn-50121939.s: Working largely on its own, Claude designed quantum circuits that improve on the best published versions, in some cases by an order of magnitude or more.
ex: Quantum computers will need carefully designed circuits to run useful algorithms on limited hardware. We gave Claude plain-language specifications for eight such circuits, drawn from chemistry, optimization, physics simulation, and number theory, along with an automated evaluator that checks and scores each design. Working largely on its own, Claude found designs that improve on the best published circuits, in some cases by an order of magnitude or more. Such improvements substantially reduce the quantum resources that useful applications require, so practical quantum computers could arrive sooner than previously anticipated. This work was led by Andi Gu as part of Anthropic’s STEM Fellows Program, with mentorship from Alek Kemeny, a quantum physicist at Anthropic, in collaboration with Susanne Yelin (Harvard University) and Mikhail Lukin (Harvard University and QuEra Computing). Read the full paper on arXiv.

hn-50118320.t: Apple ML Research: Muse Spark Open with MLX on Mac Studio
hn-50118320.s: Local and Distributed Large LLM Inference with MLX and RDMA on Mac Studio
ex: Local and Distributed Large LLM Inference with MLX and RDMA on Mac Studio MLX on Mac with Apple silicon lets AI researchers and developers experiment locally with the latest models and methods in a private environment. The open-source array framework leverages the unified memory architecture of Apple silicon, enabling anyone to run new inference and fine-tuning methods on their own hardware and explore other AI techniques. In a previous post, we highlighted the advantages of the M5 architecture and its GPU Neural Accelerators. In this post, we show how to run the latest frontier-class model — Muse Spark Open, with nearly a trillion parameters — right from your desk, using the latest version of MLX, released today. On a cluster of four Mac Studios, Muse Spark Open generates over 36 tokens per second (see Figure 1), well above average human reading speed.

hn-50112739.t: Any window from your Mac, on your iPhone and iPad
hn-50112739.s: Any window from your Mac, live on your iPhone or iPad. Touch, Apple Pencil, trackpad and keys. Free, open source, no servers.
ex: Any window from your Mac, on your iPhone and iPad. Sill shows a window from your Mac, or the whole desktop, on your iPhone or iPad. You use it there with touch, a trackpad, a keyboard or Apple Pencil. Sill for Mac captures the window, encodes it as HEVC video and sends it to the Sill app on your device. Your taps, clicks, scrolls and keys go back to your Mac. Your Mac and your device connect on the same network, over a USB cable, with Direct Wireless Connection when they share no network, or through your own VPN, such as Tailscale, with Remote Access. There is no account and no server in between. getsill.app · Download for Mac · Support · Privacy · Terms Sill for Mac is a free, notarized download from getsill.app; with Homebrew, brew install --cask saffsanity/sill/sill installs the same download from Sill's own tap. Sill for iPhone and iPad is free on the App Store, and you can also build it from source (below).

hn-50121562.t: Anthropic Console overcharged my card 100x due to internationalization input bug
hn-50121562.s: I am a LegalTech Attorney leading a developer team from Costa Rica. While trying to load credits onto my Anthropic API account (claude.com), I experienced a critical internationalization (i18n) and…
ex: I am a LegalTech Attorney leading a developer team from Costa Rica. While trying to load credits onto my Anthropic API account (claude.com), I experienced a critical internationalization (i18n) and UX failure that has placed an unfair financial burden on me due to a severe oversight in their payment pipeline. The platform prompted me for a payment. Since I am in a Spanish-speaking region where localized systems and keyboards handle dots and commas differently, I typed 5.04. Anthropic’s input system completely failed to sanitize or validate the data. Instead of throwing a formatting error or converting it properly, it silently stripped the decimal internally and instantly charged my credit card $504.00 USD instead of $5.04 USD. To make matters worse, there was no confirmation modal or review screen summarizing the final amount before processing the transaction. It was a single-click, instantaneous overcharge.

gh-1423190069.s: 🐋 Полный гайд на русском: как установить и запустить DeepSeek локально (V4, R1) на ПК, Mac и сервере — Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio, vLLM, Open WebUI, API, RAG, агенты, fine-tuning, лучшие фишки
ex: потом sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl restart ollama. llama.cpp — движок, на котором построены Ollama и LM Studio. Он первым получает поддержку новых моделей и даёт полный контроль над тем, что лежит на GPU, а что в RAM. Готовые сборки: GitHub Releases (Windows, macOS, Linux), на Mac — brew install llama.cpp. Как это работает. -ngl 99 отправляет все слои на GPU, а -ot (override-tensor) возвращает тяжёлых «экспертов» MoE в оперативную память. На видеокарте остаются внимание и общие слои, то есть то, что считается на каждом токене. Так модель на 284B работает с одной игровой картой. llama-server сразу даёт веб-чат на http://localhost:8080 и OpenAI-совместимый API на http://localhost:8080/v1. 1. Скачай с lmstudio.ai (Windows, macOS, Linux). 2. Открой поиск 🔍, введи deepseek, выбери модель и квант. Зелёная метка означает, что модель поместится в твою видеокарту. 3. Чатись во вкладке Chat, а во вкладке Developer → Start Server включается API на http://localhost:1234/v1.

gh-1422962789.s: I gave Claude Code 120 pages of my handwritten college notes. It gave me back my handwriting as a real font, in 66 minutes for $13.68.
ex: Every letter comes from the notes: it was found in the page photos, then redrawn along the pen's path with one steady ballpoint nib. Each letter has 2–3 real variants from different pages that rotate as you type, so doubled letters never look stamped. 2x speed. Full 65-second video (MP4). Every frame is real pipeline output, made with Remotion in video/. Or install it on your computer for Figma, Keynote, Word and the rest: grab HarshpreetHand-Regular.ttf and -Bold.ttf from the latest release. 1. Copy the .woff2 (and optionally .woff) files into the site, e.g. public/fonts/. 2. Copy harshpreet-hand.css next to them (or paste its rules into your global CSS) and fix the url() paths if needed. 3. Turn the theme on: document.documentElement.dataset.theme = "handwritten". Tips: - Keep line-height at 1.5 or more. The g and y loops go deep, just like in the notes. - Use it for headings and prose. Keep code, tables and dense UI in your normal fonts.
